title: The morning offering
hookLine: offering the whole day, work and joys and trouble, before it starts

cards: Your alarm goes off. Before your eyes are fully open, your hand is reaching for the phone. And in the next ninety seconds, the day gets handed out.
To the news. To the group chat. To a work email that makes your stomach drop.

To somebody's vacation photos. By the time your feet touch the floor, your day belongs to a dozen people, and you never decided to give it to any of them. There's an old Catholic habit that gets there first.
Before anything else claims the day, you give the whole thing away, on purpose, to God.

teach.b: In 1844, in a Jesuit house in the south of France, a group of young men training to be priests were restless. They wanted to be missionaries in distant countries, doing something that mattered.
Instead they were stuck with books and chores. Their spiritual director, a priest named François-Xavier Gautrelet, changed their mood.
You can be missionaries right now, he said, here. Offer everything you do today, the study, the dishes, the boredom, for the work of the Church around the world.
That became a movement called the Apostleship of Prayer, and it spread to millions. It lives on as the Pope's Worldwide Prayer Network. Its heart is a short prayer said on waking.

The words vary, but it offers to God, through the heart of Jesus, all the prayers, works, joys and sufferings of the day ahead, often joined to an intention the Pope asks people to pray for that month.
Notice what's in that list. Not just the good parts. The meeting you dread.
The kid who won't get dressed. The pain in your back. All of it, handed over before it happens.
The idea goes back to Paul. In the Douay-Rheims he asks Christians to "present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing unto God." Not a sacrifice on an altar: a whole ordinary life, offered.

teach.h: NOTHING IN THE DAY IS WASTED.
teach.b: So nothing in the day is wasted, even the parts that feel like a waste.

teach.h: PRESENT YOUR BODIES A LIVING SACRIFICE.
teach.b: Catholics would say the day is already given, so it already counts.

how: Many Catholics say a morning offering on waking, often a prayer from the Apostleship of Prayer (now the Pope's Worldwide Prayer Network) that offers the day's prayers, works, joys and sufferings, joined to the Pope's intention for the month.

games.why: Gautrelet told them to offer their study, chores and boredom for the Church's work. that became the Apostleship of Prayer.

practice: Picture waking up tomorrow: the alarm, your hand moving toward the phone, and then your hand going still, so that before anything else gets the day, you give it away first.
If you pray, you can offer the whole day to God, work, joys and trouble, in a few words of your own, or with a morning offering from a prayer book. If you don't, simply decide what the day is for.

wordCard.voice: Oblatio. Latin for an offering, a short prayer on waking that gives the whole day to God before it starts, joys and sufferings too.

orig.note: Latin: an offering, from offerre, to carry toward. English oblation comes from it.

carryVoice: Your line: today is already given. Even ten seconds, before the phone gets it, is enough to give it away. Until tomorrow.
